newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan TSE opens way for Chinese companies to list.
newsitem.headline: Japan TSE opens way for Chinese companies to list.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Tuesday it had formally signed a pact with the China Securities Regulatory Commission making it possible for Chinese companies to list on the Tokyo bourse.

The Finance Ministry, meanwhile, said it signed a memorandum with the Chinese commission to cooperate in sharing information on securities and derivatives markets, completing all preparatory steps for the listing of Chinese firms.

Japanese media reported that Chinese firms such as Tianjin Automobile Industrial Co Ltd and Huabei Pharmaceuticals Group Co Ltd are likely to be the first to be listed on the TSE following the agreement, applying as early as this year.
In December, the official Xinhua news agency reported that the Chinese government had approved 38 firms for listing shares on stock markets abroad, without specifying which exchanges.

It said the securities commission under the State Council had approved the Beijing Yanshan Petrochemical Co and China Great Wall Computer Group Co among the 38 firms on the long-awaited list of China's fourth such batch.

Tokyo brokers said permitting Chinese firms to list on the bourse was yet another step towards the internationalisation of the TSE, but added that it was still too early to discern how the shares would be received by Japanese investors.
"Whether or not the shares gather attention or not depends on the share itself or the industry it represents," said Kenji Karikome of Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.

Worried over a series of defections by foreign companies, mainly due to the high cost of maintaining a listing in Japan, the TSE and the Osaka Securities Exchange have stepped up their efforts to lure foreign firms to Japanese markets.
Late last year, the Osaka bourse set up an Asian stock section targeting medium-sized companies from the region.
The head of the Tokyo exchange went to China recently to urge companies there to consider Tokyo rather than other major international markets.
At present 66 foreign firms are listed on the TSE. In the last five years, 61 foreign firms have delisted from the TSE, while only three firms have come in, according to TSE data.
The latest entry is Hong Kong's Henderson Land Development Co Ltd, which last month became only the second Asian company based outside Japan to list on the bourse.
